title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: RAG retrieves relevant evidence at request time and gives that evidence to a language model so the answer can be grounded and cited.

title: Embeddings and vector search
text: Embeddings represent meaning as numeric vectors. Nearest-neighbor search can retrieve semantically similar passages even when they use different words.

title: Document chunking
text: Chunking divides a document into retrievable units. Chunk boundaries and size affect whether the necessary evidence can be found.

title: Reranking
text: A reranker applies a more precise relevance model to a small candidate set after the first retrieval pass.

title: RAG evaluation
text: Retrieval and generation should be evaluated separately. Useful retrieval measures include recall at k, precision, and ranking quality.

title: Agents and tools
text: An AI agent uses a model to choose bounded actions, call tools, observe results, and stop when its goal or limit is reached.

title: Prompt injection and guardrails
text: Retrieved content is untrusted input. A prompt injection inside a document must not be treated as an instruction with system authority.

title: Caching
text: Caching can reduce repeated model cost and latency, but cache keys and invalidation must account for model, prompt, and data versions.

title: AI observability
text: Production traces should expose retrieval results, model latency, token usage, errors, and evaluation status without recording secrets.

title: Fine-tuning
text: Fine-tuning updates model behavior or capabilities through training examples. It is not a replacement for retrieving frequently changing facts.
